> 其安易持，其未兆易謀。其脆易泮，其微易散.

Chapter 63 said: draw the difficulty while it is still easy. Chapter 64 pushes the camera one step further back — to the moment before there is anything to draw.

## 兆 is a crack burned into a shell

兆: 灼龜坼也 — the split that opens when you burn a tortoise shell.

The procedure was exact: a small hole drilled in the plastron, a fire underneath, and the burning continued until the shell broke with a sound. The crack that appeared was the 兆. Only once it had split could fortune be read.

So 未兆 is not "before the signs appeared." Signs mean the thing is already there and you have just now seen it.

未兆 means: it has not split yet. It does not know yet which way it will go.

## 其未兆易謀

Therefore the instruction is not "act while the signs are small." It is: act while it has not yet cracked — while it is still possible to decide what shape the crack takes.

That is a much narrower window than most people think, and a much more powerful one.

## 泮 is half water, half wall

泮: 冰釋也, and also 分也 — the ice letting go, the thing dividing.

其脆易泮 — what is brittle splits easily. The brittleness is not a weakness to be fixed; it is the state in which a division is cheap.

其微易散 — what is fine disperses easily.

Four states, and each is a window: 安 (settled), 未兆 (uncracked), 脆 (brittle), 微 (fine). Each is easier to handle than what follows it.

## 為之於未有，治之於未亂

Act on what does not yet exist; order what is not yet disordered.

The compression is total: the object of the action is not there yet. That is the definition of working early, and it is why early work is so hard to justify — there is nothing to point at.

## The three images

合抱之木，生於毫末 — a tree you cannot encircle began at a hair's tip.
九層之臺，起於累土 — a nine-tier terrace began with one basket of earth.
千里之行，始於足下 — a thousand-li journey begins under the foot.

Three scales, and each names the same gap: the beginning is not a small version of the end. A hair tip is not a small tree.

## 為者敗之，執者失之

The one who acts fails it; the one who grips loses it.

The line is not a prohibition on action. It is the report of a specific error: acting on what has not yet cracked, and gripping what has no handle. Chapter 56 removed the handle; here the grip is what loses.

## 民之從事，常於幾成而敗之

People's undertakings usually fail at 幾成 — when they are nearly complete.

幾 is the almost. Not failure at the start, where caution is high, and not failure after completion — failure at the point where the outcome is visible enough to be wanted.

## 慎終如始，則無敗事

Be as careful at the end as at the beginning, and nothing fails.

The asymmetry is real: at the start there is no stake, so care is cheap; at the end the stake is everything, and care has to be chosen.

## 欲不欲，不貴難得之貨；學不學，復眾人之所過

Want the not-wanting; do not price the rare goods. Learn the not-learning; return to what the crowd has passed over.

復 is to go back over — to retrace. 眾人之所過 is what everyone stepped past: the ordinary, the unremarkable, the thing that was too plain to pick up.

## 以輔萬物之自然而不敢為

輔: 人頰車也 — the cheekbone, the jaw plate inside the face.

The image is the chapter's best. Teeth do not grow out of the jaw; they grow themselves. The jaw does one thing: gives each tooth a place and holds it there.

《左傳》 has 輔車相依，唇亡齒寒 — cheekbone and jaw rely on each other; when the lips go, the teeth are cold.

So 輔萬物之自然 is: be the jaw. Not make the tooth — hold the position where the tooth can come in.

And 不敢為 closes it: the whole chapter's early action is not manufacturing. It is providing a place, at the moment when a place still decides something.

## A test

Take one thing that went wrong for you in the last year. Find the moment it had not yet cracked — before anyone could see it, including you. What would holding a place there have required?
